steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Embellishment adds surface detail: beading, sequins, embroidery, quilting — each creates different textural and visual effects.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Felting mats fibres together: wet felting uses soap, water and friction; needle felting uses barbed needles to interlock fibres.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Heat manipulation of synthetic fabrics can create permanent sculptural forms — crumpling, pleating, melting.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Mixed media textiles break boundaries by incorporating non-traditional materials: paper, wire, plastic, found objects.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring embellishment and mixed media textiles. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with embellishment and mixed media textiles. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with embellishment and mixed media textiles. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to embellishment and mixed media textiles, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to r | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
